confirm.stopDesc: Deletes the K8s Job to release the GPUs. The record and config are kept: you can clone it and run it again, but it cannot be resumed.
confirm.deleteDescList: This also deletes the K8s Job and its Pods.
confirm.deleteDescDetail: This also deletes the K8s Job and its Pods, and cannot be undone.

messages.stopped: Training job stopped (GPUs released; the record and config are kept, so you can clone it to run again)

list.description: Multi-node GPU training jobs based on the HyperPod Training Operator, with Kueue queueing and topology-aware scheduling.
list.filterHint: Filtering is limited to the latest 5000 items.

tips.status: The training job's own runtime status (CR phase). Running: running; Suspended: held by Kueue while waiting for quota; Complete: training finished; Failed: failed; and so on. Click the magnifier for the full status details.
tips.queueStatus: The training job's status in the Kueue scheduling queue (separate from its own status). Queued: waiting for quota; Admitted: admitted by Kueue; Evicted: preempted and sent back to the queue; and so on.
tips.spec: Resources requested by the training job: number of nodes × GPUs per node. Hover over the tag to see the CPU cores and memory per node. Multi-node training communicates over NCCL/EFA.

suspended.label: Suspended by Kueue
suspended.detail: spec.suspend=true, so the Operator does not create Pods. Common right after submission when the quota is full. Once Kueue admits the job it is unsuspended automatically and moves to Created/Running.

created.label: Created (Pods queued / starting)
created.detail: The Operator has unsuspended the job and created its child resources (Pods / networking), but not all of them are Running yet. Pods may be pulling images, waiting for nodes, SchedulingGated, and so on.

podsRunning.label: All Pods ready
podsRunning.detail: A replica-check state set by the operator: all worker Pods are Running and ready. (Running is at the Job level; PodsRunning is at the Pod level.)

running.detail: All Pods are Running and the training process is running. Running is shown on its own only after the Operator has set Created to False.

faulted.label: Faulted (HyperPod auto-resume in progress)
faulted.detail: A Pod is unhealthy (node lost, OOM, CUDA error, and so on) and HyperPod is attempting auto-resume (3 retries by default). On success the job returns to Running; otherwise it moves to Failed.

completed.detail: Same as Complete; an alias used by different Operator versions. The backend treats the two identically (the substring "Complete" marks either one as a terminal state).

failed.detail: Terminal state: auto-resume has used up its retries and the job still failed, or the training code exited with a non-zero exit code. Check the Pod logs, or the reason/message in the "Status timeline" card.

pods.title: Current Pods ({{total}})
pods.empty: No Pods yet (the Job was just created and has not been scheduled)

basic.displayNameTooltip: Also used as the prefix of the K8s job name, so it must be a valid DNS name: start with a lowercase letter, be 3-29 characters long, contain only a-z, 0-9 and '-', and end with a letter or digit. For notes in other languages such as Chinese, use the "Description" field below. The final job name = this name + '-' + 10 random characters, generated by the backend at creation.

basic.displayNamePattern: Must start with a lowercase letter, contain only a-z, 0-9 and '-', and end with a letter or digit.

resource.noTypesInPool: No instance types available in this resource pool

resource.templatePlaceholder: Select a resource template (maintained by admins)
resource.noTemplates: No resource templates yet · ask a Workspace admin to create one in Admin Console → Resource Template
resource.nodeCountTooltip: Multi-node distributed training (DDP); HyperPodPyTorchJob replicas. The number of nodes is not capped for thousand-GPU training; it is limited by quota and scheduling.
resource.sparesTooltip: Request a few extra nodes to take over when a node fails (HyperPodPyTorchJob spares). These nodes are actually started and count against your quota; they are not idle standbys. Which nodes take part in training is decided by the training script reading NSPARES.
resource.perNodeSpecTooltip: GPU/CPU/memory are governed by the resource template and cannot be entered manually; switching templates syncs them automatically.

topology.title: Topology-aware scheduling (TAS · optional)
topology.help: g6 nodes are not on the TAS support list (only p3dn/p4d/p5+/trn take effect). Selecting an unsupported type such as g6.12xlarge does not raise an error; K8s silently ignores it and it simply has no effect.
topology.modeTooltip: preferred = prefer the same level and fall back to a higher one / required = must be the same level, wait until available / none = no constraint
topology.levelTooltip: The available levels are determined by the Topology linked to the ResourceFlavor of this instance type (read from the cluster), listed from finest to coarsest.
topology.noLevels: This instance type has no selectable topology levels
topology.noLevelsShort: No selectable levels for this instance type

resource.priorityTooltip: Only platform admins can change the priority class of a task.

launch.scriptHelp: Write the entire launch script directly. The platform runs it as-is (you fully control the distributed launch and call hyperpodrun yourself). NNODES / NPROC_PER_NODE / JOB_NAME are already injected at the container level. See the examples on the right.
launch.scriptLabel: Script content (written directly; the whole script is the launch command)
launch.scriptTooltip:
The platform runs the whole script as-is, and you fully control the distributed launch (call hyperpodrun yourself)
You can also write a single line that runs a script on FSx, for example bash /fsx/.../run.sh
NNODES / NPROC_PER_NODE / JOB_NAME are already injected into the container
Two examples on the right (open the drawer to view them): "hyperpodrun example" shows how to write the distributed launch yourself; "Wrapped command example" puts your command into a payload and lets the platform host it
launch.exampleWrapDesc: Read-only reference · your command goes into a PAYLOAD heredoc, and the platform hosts it with hyperpodrun --no-python and passes the exit code through. Only tasks wrapped with hyperpodrun are supported for now.
launch.exampleDefaultDesc: Read-only reference · you fully control the distributed launch (call hyperpodrun yourself). NNODES / NPROC_PER_NODE / JOB_NAME are already injected at the container level.
launch.envHelp: NNODES / NPROC_PER_NODE / JOB_NAME are injected automatically at the container level (use $JOB_NAME and so on directly in the script; do not set them here, because they are reserved by the operator and will be rejected). Enter your own variables here, such as WANDB_PROJECT.
launch.envReserved: NNODES/NPROC_PER_NODE/JOB_NAME are reserved by the operator; do not set them.
launch.secretHelp: Pick keys you created in "Secret management"; they are injected as environment variables with the same name (values are never written into the config in plain text; they go through secretKeyRef). The env name equals the key name.
launch.secretPlaceholder: Select a Secret key (= environment variable name)
launch.secretEmpty: No keys available (add one on the Secret management page first)

scripts.inline:
#!/bin/bash
# ============================================================
# Training launch script (inline) · the platform runs it as-is, and you fully control the distributed launch
# Environment variables injected at the container level: NNODES / NPROC_PER_NODE / JOB_NAME
# Change TRAIN_SCRIPT to your training entry point (a .py file on FSx)
# ============================================================
set -e

echo "NPROC_PER_NODE: ${NPROC_PER_NODE}"
echo "NNODES:         ${NNODES}"
echo "JOB_NAME:       ${JOB_NAME}"
echo "Hostname:       $(hostname)"
echo "============================================="

# Install the hyperpod elastic agent (provides hyperpodrun)
pip install --upgrade hyperpod-elastic-agent

hyperpodrun \
    --nnodes=${NNODES} \
    --nproc-per-node=${NPROC_PER_NODE} \
    --server-host=0.0.0.0 \
    --server-port=8080 \
    --server-log-level=warning \
    --tee=3 \
    --log_dir=/tmp/hyperpod \
    ${TRAIN_SCRIPT} \
        --total-epochs 200 \
        --save-every 2 \
        --batch-size 32 \
        --snapshot-path /fsx/hyperpodrun-elastic-ddp/${JOB_NAME}.snapshot.pt
scripts.wrap:
set +e
bash <<'PAYLOAD'
# ↓↓↓ Your command ↓↓↓
echo "hello from scientist"
sleep 20
# ↑↑↑ End of your command; it may exit 0 or non-zero ↑↑↑
PAYLOAD
rc=$?
echo "[platform] payload exited rc=$rc -> deliver completion signal"
command -v hyperpodrun >/dev/null || pip install -q hyperpod-elastic-agent
exec hyperpodrun --nnodes=1 --nproc-per-node=1 \
  --server-host=0.0.0.0 --server-port=8080 \
  --no-python bash -c "exit $rc"
